parts.text:
{
  "extractions": [
    {
      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F001"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking FMLA eligibility.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F002",
          "F003",
          "F004"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "All three requirements must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F002:F004",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801",
          "§ 825.105(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (referencing § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005",
          "F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted, subject to paragraph (b)(2) exceptions.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not be",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005",
          "F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "need not be counted",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F006",
          "F007"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where the employee has had a break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be counted",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F008:F009",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (1) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (2) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing purposes)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F008"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when an employee has a period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F007"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "must be also counted",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "USERRA"
        ],
        "statement": "The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F008",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F008"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to section 825.110 provisions addressing USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "USERRA"
        ],
        "statement": "Section 825.110 does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F010"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies if an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F010"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F011"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "Nothing in this section prevents",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Nothing in section 825.110 prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F011"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies if an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (c)(2)",
          "§ 825.801",
          "29 CFR part 785"
        ],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), with the determining factor being the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is not limited by methods of recordkeeping, or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all of the hours an employee has worked for or been in service to the employer."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when determining actual hours worked under FLSA principles.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "USERRA",
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, and a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has the hours that would have been worked added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "can generally",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's requirement that a record be kept of their hours worked (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees as defined in 29 CFR part 541).",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "29 CFR part 541"
        ],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked, in order to claim that an employee (such as a full-time teacher) is not eligible for FMLA leave.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate, for example, that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the teachers are not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F015"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start (referencing § 825.300(b) for employee eligibility notice rules)."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F015"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when an employee meets the 12-month eligibility requirement while on non-FMLA leave.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may",
        "modality": "possible",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies to ascertaining whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles for an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, for that specific notice of the need for leave.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Applies when an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles, but the employer expects the count to drop below 50 by the time leave begins.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles (e.g., 60 employees in August) for a period of leave to begin later (e.g., in December), even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December)."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee of a covered employer seeking FMLA eligibility.
unit_attributes.choice_text: All three requirements must be satisfied: (1) employed by the employer for at least 12 months; AND (2) employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave; AND (3) employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave (referencing § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees), and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite (referencing § 825.105(b) for employees outside the U.S.).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted, subject to paragraph (b)(2) exceptions.
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided that employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted subject to the exceptions in paragraph (b)(2).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section.
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies in determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, where the employee has had a break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation; OR (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where either: (1) the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of a Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation; or (2) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service (e.g., for education or childrearing purposes).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employee has a period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: The period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed for at least 12 months by the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to section 825.110 provisions addressing USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: Section 825.110 does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under the USERRA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.).
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (e.g., workers' compensation, group health plan benefits, etc.), the week counts as a week of employment.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies for purposes of determining whether intermittent, occasional, or casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: For purposes of determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months, 52 weeks is deemed to be equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employer determines whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing in section 825.110 prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies if an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years, the employer must do so uniformly, with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section and in § 825.801 containing the special hours of service requirement for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and in § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to the principles established under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) for determining compensable hours of work (see 29 CFR part 785), with the determining factor being the number of hours an employee has worked for the employer within the meaning of the FLSA.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is not limited by methods of recordkeeping, or by compensation agreements that do not accurately reflect all of the hours an employee has worked for or been in service to the employer.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when determining actual hours worked under FLSA principles.
unit_attributes.statement: Any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA's principles may be used to determine whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to an employee returning from or reemployed following USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service in determining eligibility for FMLA-qualifying leave, and a person reemployed following USERRA-covered service has the hours that would have been worked added to any hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (referencing § 825.801(c) for airline flight crew employees).
unit_attributes.statement: In order to determine the hours that would have been worked during the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service, the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees who are exempt from FLSA's requirement that a record be kept of their hours worked (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees as defined in 29 CFR part 541).
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including for employees exempt from FLSA recordkeeping requirements (e.g., bona fide executive, administrative, and professional employees defined in 29 CFR part 541), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked, in order to claim that an employee (such as a full-time teacher) is not eligible for FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must be able to clearly demonstrate, for example, that full-time teachers (defined in § 825.102) of an elementary or secondary school system, institution of higher education, or other educational establishment did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the teachers are not eligible for FMLA leave (referencing § 825.801(d) for airline flight crew employees).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to the determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start (referencing § 825.300(b) for employee eligibility notice rules).

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an employee meets the 12-month eligibility requirement while on non-FMLA leave.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee may be on non-FMLA leave at the time he or she meets the 12-month eligibility requirement, and in that event, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after the employee meets the eligibility requirement would be FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies to ascertaining whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles for an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain an employee's eligibility for FMLA benefits is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, whether the leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, for that specific notice of the need for leave.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether leave is to be taken at one time or on an intermittent or reduced leave schedule basis, once an employee is determined eligible in response to a notice of the need for leave, the employee's eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in the number of employees employed at or within 75 miles of the employee's worksite, for that specific notice of the need for leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when employee leave has already started and the employee count drops below 50.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Applies when an otherwise eligible employee gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles, but the employer expects the count to drop below 50 by the time leave begins.
unit_attributes.statement: An employer must grant FMLA benefits to an otherwise eligible employee who gives notice of the need for leave when 50 or more employees are employed within 75 miles (e.g., 60 employees in August) for a period of leave to begin later (e.g., in December), even if the employer expects that the number of employees will drop below 50 (e.g., to 40 in December).
